objective: Build and diagnose a bounded loop that executes tool requests, returns matching results, and finishes with an answer supported by those results.
audience: People who use AI assistants and can read simple loops and objects.
prerequisites: Read a function call, condition, loop, and object field. No model API experience is required.
scenario: A support assistant needs current inventory counts for a customer. The model can ask for a lookup; the application must run it and supply the result.

steps.purpose: Establish the user task, three responsibilities, and the meaning of a tool request and conversation.
Inspect a complete working loop, with real engine events, code, and message history side by side.
Predict and observe a loop with one missing operation before receiving its explanation.
Repair result handling using the evidence from the preceding experiment.
Compare a matching request/result pair with an unrelated ID. Explain who executes a tool.
Diagnose a loop that produces a request but no tool result.
Distinguish the answer branch from the call limit. Derive the call budget for the simulated policy.
Repair a loop that continues after receiving a final answer.
Apply message matching and budget reasoning to a new broken loop and requests of different lengths.
Reconnect the code to each responsibility and explain what changes with a real model adapter.
Change one operation at a time and explain the difference using trace evidence.

concepts.explanation: A client tool request describes a function and inputs; the application executes it.
A tool result held in a local variable is absent from the next model input until the application adds it.
The result must retain the identifier of the request it answers.
Returning an answer completes the task; reaching a limit can stop unfinished work.

misconceptions.belief: The model runs a tool by naming it.
misconceptions.feedback: A model request followed by a stop has no tool execution event.

misconceptions.belief: A successful function call automatically informs the model.
misconceptions.feedback: The tool event has output, while the conversation has no result message.

misconceptions.belief: Any stock value in the conversation answers the request.
misconceptions.feedback: Compare the request ID with the result callId; matching item names alone are insufficient in this protocol.

misconceptions.belief: A stopped loop means the task succeeded.
misconceptions.feedback: Inspect whether the application returned an answer or merely exhausted its call budget.

transfer.task: Repair a new loop so one program answers all inventory requests within eight model calls.
changes: A result is present with an unrelated call ID, unlike the missing result in practice.
The requests contain two or three items in different orders, so three calls do not suffice for every case.
transfer.withheldGuidance: The task states outcomes and constraints. It does not identify faulty fields or name the correct options. Hints and solution are separate.

claimSources.claim: For client tools, the application executes model requests and returns results.
The result is associated with the tool request it answers. Our field names are a simplified teaching protocol.
Agent loops use tool feedback and stopping conditions. The exact call-count formula is specific to our engine.
